extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant peer reviewers and applicants preparing RPG (R01/R03/R15/R21/R34) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and reviewer guidance for evaluating Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), describing the criteria reviewers must use and program-specific expectations for scoring and critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R15 variant: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to make an important scientific contribution to the research field(s) involved, to provide research opportunities to students, and to strengthen the research environment of the institution, in consideration of the review criteria and additional review criteria. Overall impact is a summary judgment based on all review criteria and any additional applicable considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If the aims of the project are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will successful completion of the aims change the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R15 addition: If funded, will the AREA award have a substantial effect on the school/academic component in terms of strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research?

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or New Investigators, or in the early stages of independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)? If the project is collaborative or multi-PD/PI, do the investigators have complementary and integrated expertise; are their leadership approach, governance and organizational structure appropriate for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R15 addition: Do the PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience in supervising students in research?

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions? Are the concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions novel to one field of research or novel in a broad sense? Is a refinement, improvement, or new application of theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions proposed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed work introduces new paradigms or represents a meaningful departure from existing methods or concepts; novelty may be incremental (refinement) or transformative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims of the project? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented? If the project is in the early stages of development, will the strategy establish feasibility and will particularly risky aspects be managed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project involves clinical research, evaluate: 1) protection of human subjects from research risks, and 2) inclusion of minorities and members of both sexes/genders, as well as inclusion of children, justified in terms of scientific goals and research strategy. R15 addition: Does the application provide sufficient evidence that the project can stimulate the interests of students so that they consider a career in the biomedical or behavioral sciences?

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are the institutional support, equipment and other physical resources available to the investigators adequate for the project proposed? Will the project benefit from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R15 focus: Are the institutional support, equipment and other physical resources adequate? Does the application demonstrate the likely availability of well-qualified students to participate? Does it provide evidence that students have in the past or are likely to pursue careers in the biomedical or behavioral sciences?

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that involves human subjects but does not involve one of the six categories of research that are exempt under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk relating to their participation according to the following five review criteria: 1) risk to subjects, 2) adequacy of protection against risks, 3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, 4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and 5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research that meets exemption criteria, committee will evaluate: 1) the justification for the exemption, 2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and 3) sources of materials. Reviewers are referred to the Human Subjects Protection and Inclusion Guidelines for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves clinical research, the committee will evaluate the proposed plans for inclusion of minorities and members of both genders, as well as the inclusion of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional information to assist determinations, reviewers should refer to the Human Subjects Protection and Inclusion Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals as part of the scientific assessment according to the following five points: 1) proposed use of the animals, and species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers to be used; 2) justifications for the use of animals and for the appropriateness of the species and numbers proposed; 3) adequacy of veterinary care; 4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury to that which is unavoidable in the conduct of scientifically sound research including the use of analgesic, anesthetic, and tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices; and 5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with the AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consult the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment, and if needed, determine whether adequate protection is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider biosafety, containment, training, and any institutional plans to mitigate hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the applicant adequately addressed prior criticisms and whether revisions materially improve the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate past productivity, outcomes relative to aims, and the justification for continued support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision application relates to a specific line of investigation presented in the original application that was not recommended for approval, then the committee will consider whether the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through the use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the foreign setting provides unique scientific advantages that justify funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided in this section of the application, including 1) the Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research, 2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, 3) the procedures that will be used to monitor possession use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and 4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate completeness and adequacy of institutional and procedural safeguards for select agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the following Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing the following types of resources, are reasonable: 1) Data Sharing Plan; 2) Sharing Model Organisms; and 3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on reasonableness of plans or justifications for not sharing; consider community benefit and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess cost realism, justification for personnel and resources, and whether the period requested matches the scope and timeline of the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These comments can include actionable suggestions, highlight weaknesses, or advise on the necessity of substantial revision prior to resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant) Program-specific Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding. Because the research project usually is limited, an R03 grant application may not contain extensive detail or discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach to the problem. Appropriate justification for the proposed work can be provided through literature citations, data from other sources, or from investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly in applications proposing pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) Program-specific Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectives of the R15 program are to (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen the research environment of schools that have not been major recipients of NIH support, and (3) expose available undergraduate and graduate students in such environments to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required for R15 application; however, they may be included if available. Review emphasis includes strengthening the institution's research environment and student exposure to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) Program-specific Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R21 exploratory/developmental grant supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies that have the potential for significant impact on biomedical or biobehavioral research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An R21 grant application need not have extensive background material or preliminary information. Accordingly, reviewers will focus their evaluation on the conceptual framework, the level of innovation, and the potential to significantly advance our knowledge or understanding. Preliminary data are not required for R21 applications; however, they may be included if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (Clinical Trial Planning Grant) Program-specific Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Clinical Trial Planning Grant Program (R34) supports development of Phase III clinical trials, including establishment of the research team, development of tools for data management and research oversight, definition of recruitment strategies, finalization of the protocol, and preparation of an operations/procedures manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Clinical Trial Planning Grant is not designed for the collection of preliminary data or the conduct of pilot studies to support the rationale for a clinical trial. Accordingly, reviewers will focus their evaluation on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol of the proposed trial in its current, early form.
